props.gloss_en: Rav Chisda: any dream, and not a fast
Rav Chisda: a dream not interpreted is like a letter not read
Rav Chisda: neither a good dream nor a bad dream is wholly fulfilled
Rav Chisda: a bad dream is better than a good dream
Rav Chisda: a bad dream -- its sadness suffices it; a good dream -- its joy suffices it
Rav Yosef: a good dream, even for me, its joy dissipates it
Rav Chisda: a bad dream is harder than lashes
his source: 'and God has made it so that they fear before Him' (Eccl 3:14)
R' Yochanan: this [that which makes men fear before Him] is a bad dream

RSBY (on Jer 23:28 'what has the straw to do with the grain', after the stam's 'what have grain and straw to do with a dream?'): just as there cannot be grain without straw, so there cannot be a dream without idle matters
R' Berekhya: a dream, even though part of it is fulfilled, the whole of it is not fulfilled
from where? from Joseph, as it is written: 'and behold, the sun and the moon [and eleven stars bowed to me]' (Gen 37:9)
and at that hour his mother was not [alive]
R' Levi: a person should always await [the fulfilment of] a good dream up to twenty-two years

from where? from Joseph: 'Joseph, being seventeen years old' (Gen 37:2) and 'Joseph was thirty years old when he stood before Pharaoh' (Gen 41:46) -- seventeen to thirty is thirteen, and seven of plenty and two of famine: twenty-two
Rav Huna: a good man is not shown a good dream
Rav Huna: and a bad man is not shown a bad dream
the baraita: all of David's years he did not see a good dream
the baraita: and all of Ahitophel's years he did not see a bad dream
R' Yirmeya bar Abba: 'no evil shall befall you' (Ps 91:10) -- neither bad dreams nor bad thoughts will frighten you
R' Yirmeya bar Abba: 'nor shall any plague come near your tent' -- you will not find your wife a doubtful nidda when you come from the road
first answer: he [David] does not see [dreams]; others see [them] for him
R' Zeira: whoever sleeps seven days without a dream is called 'evil'
his source: 'and he who is sated shall lodge, he shall not be visited by evil' (Prov 19:23)
read not save'a ('sated') but sheva ('seven') (אל תקרי)
rather, this is what it [the baraita] says: he saw, and did not know what he saw
R' Yochanan (as first reported): one who sees a dream and his soul is distressed should go and have it interpreted before three
R' Yochanan (as emended): he should better it before three

let him bring three and say to them 'I saw a good dream'; and they say to him 'it is good and let it be good, may the Merciful make it good; seven times may they decree on you from heaven that it be good, and it will be good'; and they say three reversals, three redemptions and three peaces
the three reversals: Ps 30:12, Jer 31:12, Deut 23:6
the three redemptions: Ps 55:19, Isa 35:10, I Sam 14:45
the three peaces: Isa 57:19, I Chron 12:19, I Sam 25:6
one who saw a dream and does not know what he saw should stand before the priests at the time they spread their hands, and say thus:

the prayer: 'Master of the world, I am Yours and my dreams are Yours... if they are good, strengthen them like Joseph's dreams; if they need healing, heal them [like Mara's waters, Miriam, Hezekiah, Jericho's waters]... as You turned Balaam's curse to blessing, so turn all my dreams to good'
and he concludes together with the priests, so that the congregation answers amen
and if not, let him say: 'Mighty on high, dwelling in power, You are peace and Your name is peace; may it be Your will to set peace upon us'

one who enters a town and fears the evil eye should take the thumb of his right hand in his left hand and the thumb of his left in his right, and say: 'I, so-and-so son of so-and-so, come of the seed of Joseph'
[the seed of Joseph,] over whom the evil eye has no dominion
as it is said: 'Joseph is a fruitful bough, a fruitful bough by a spring (alei ayin)' (Gen 49:22)
read not alei ayin ('by a spring') but olei ayin ('rising above the eye') (אל תקרי)

R' Yosei b'R' Chanina: from here -- 'and let them multiply like fish in the midst of the land' (Gen 48:16): as water covers the fish of the sea and the evil eye has no dominion over them, so over Joseph's seed the evil eye has no dominion
and if he fears his own evil eye, let him look at the side of his left nostril
one who falls ill should not reveal it on the first day, so that his fortune not be harmed; from then on, let him reveal it

Rava, when he fell ill, did not reveal it the first day; from then on he told his attendant: go out and announce 'Rava is ill' -- whoever loves me, let him ask mercy for me, and whoever hates me, let him rejoice over me
and it is written: 'rejoice not when your enemy falls... lest the Lord see it and it displease Him, and He turn away His wrath from him' (Prov 24:17-18)
Shmuel, when he saw a bad dream, would say: 'and dreams speak falsely' (Zech 10:2)
when he saw a good dream he would say: do dreams speak falsely? is it not written: 'in a dream I speak with him' (Num 12:6)?
Rava set 'in a dream I speak with him' against 'and dreams speak falsely' and resolved: here [the true dream] is by means of an angel
...here [the false dream] is by means of a demon

R' Bena'a: there were twenty-four interpreters of dreams in Jerusalem; once I dreamed a dream and went to all of them; what one interpreted for me the other did not, and all of them were fulfilled in me
R' Bena'a: to fulfil what is said: 'all dreams follow the mouth'
R' Elazar: [that] all dreams follow the mouth -- from where?
as it is said: 'and as he interpreted to us, so it was' (Gen 41:13)
Rava: and that is when it is interpreted for him in keeping with his dream (a restriction of R' Elazar's principle)
as it is said: 'to each according to his dream he interpreted' (Gen 41:12)

R' Elazar (answering the stam's 'the chief baker saw [that he interpreted well] -- how did he know?', Gen 40:16): this teaches that each was shown his own dream and the interpretation of his fellow's dream
R' Yochanan: one who rose early and a verse fell into his mouth -- this is a minor prophecy
R' Yochanan: three dreams are fulfilled -- a dream of the morning
...and a dream his fellow dreamed about him
...and a dream interpreted within a dream
and some say: also a dream that is repeated
as it is said: 'and because the dream was repeated [to Pharaoh twice, the thing is established by God]' (Gen 41:32)
R' Yonatan: a person is shown [in a dream] only from the thoughts of his heart
as it is said: 'you, O king, your thoughts came up upon your bed' (Dan 2:29)
and if you wish, say from here: 'and that you may know the thoughts of your heart' (Dan 2:30)
Rava: know [that it is so], for a person is shown neither a palm tree of gold nor an elephant going through the eye of a needle

objections.gloss_en: והכתיב: לא תאנה אליך רעה, and R' Yirmeya bar Abba read it: no bad dreams will frighten you -- so how could David have seen [only bad dreams]?

answered_by.gloss_en: אלא איהו לא חזי ליה, אחריני חזו ליה (= p_acherim_chazu) -- this first answer is attacked at 55b.6 (obj_vechi_lo_chaza) and abandoned (אלא)
אלא הכי קאמר: דחזא ולא ידע מאי חזא (= p_chaza_velo_yada) -- the standing answer

objections.gloss_en: וכי לא חזא איהו מעליותא הוא? והאמר רבי זירא: כל הלן שבעה ימים בלא חלום נקרא רע -- is not seeing any dream a virtue?

יפתרנו?! והאמר רב חסדא: חלמא דלא מפשר כאגרתא דלא מקריא -- interpreting a distressing dream would bring about its fulfilment; the stam's response is to emend the dictum (אלא אימא יטיבנו), conceding the wording
אטו כל החלומות הולכים אחר הפה קרא הוא? -- R' Bena'a cites it as מה שנאמר; is it a verse?

answered_by.gloss_en: אין, וכדרבי אלעזר -- yes: R' Elazar derives it from Gen 41:13
